questions.stem: Which ion movement causes the rapid depolarization phase of a typical neuronal action potential?

questions.stem: An impulse travels 0.8 m along an axon in 0.02 s. What is its average conduction speed?
options: 40 m s⁻¹
4 m s⁻¹
400 m s⁻¹
questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 0.8 ÷ 0.02 = 40 m s⁻¹. The units are metres per second, not seconds per metre.

questions.explanation: Calcium entry at the terminal triggers vesicle fusion. Blocking that entry reduces transmitter release even though the impulse has reached the terminal.

questions.stem: A stronger stimulus produces more action potentials per second in the same sensory axon. The height of individual action potentials stays approximately constant. This illustrates:

Larger action potentials encoding every stronger stimulus
A complete loss of the refractory period
Stimulus intensity encoded mainly by impulse frequency in that axon
questions.explanation: Action potentials are approximately all-or-none events. Within the axon’s operating limits, a stronger stimulus can increase frequency rather than individual impulse amplitude.
